elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 10.5: "This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York ... without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws." Untouched by the redline.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Inserted Venue sentence: "Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over the merits of any dispute ... provided that either Party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief only, so the exclusive merits forum survives; mutual direction and no arbitration seat is introduced.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The operative language keeps New York law; no Delaware, California, or England and Wales choice of law appears. (Not a defect: the preferred level is satisfied.)

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The inserted forum is New York County, New York, not Delaware, California, or London courts. (Not a defect: the preferred level is satisfied.)

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the retained sentence supplies New York law and the single inserted sentence supplies exclusive New York County merits jurisdiction with only the customary temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out.

Minimality holds: the governing-law sentence is preserved verbatim (including the conflict-of-laws exclusion), nothing outside the checklist is deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (fee-shifting, jury waiver, service-of-process, arbitration, survival tails) are added. Because the document contained no forum provision, a concise insertion of wholly new words is permissible.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references, or contradictory retained sentences; the new clause is captioned separately and does not disturb remedies, timing, or commercial mechanics elsewhere.

Finding status of deviation is defensible on the operative facts: the law was acceptable but no forum existed anywhere, so neither the preferred nor the fallback forum element was met before the edit. Note in the rationale that the pre-existing governing-law selection was already at the preferred position and was not redlined.
